facts.text: Model-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop run braking logic entirely in a computer.
facts.quote: Model-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop run the braking logic entirely in a computer.

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop connects the real control unit to a simulated machine.
facts.quote: Hardware-in-the-loop connects the real control unit to a simulated machine.

facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop puts a real machine on a test track and feeds the machine simulated obstacles.
facts.quote: Vehicle-in-the-loop puts a real machine on a test track and feeds it simulated obstacles.

facts.text: Proving-ground tests use real machines and soft targets.
facts.quote: Proving-ground tests use real machines and soft targets.

facts.text: Shadow mode runs the system on real sites with the brakes disconnected and counts what the system would have done.
facts.quote: Shadow mode runs the system on real sites with the brakes disconnected, counting what it would have done.

facts.text: Staged release initially switches braking on only for a narrow set of machines and situations.
facts.quote: Staged release switches braking on for a narrow set of machines and situations first.

facts.text: Each successive rung of the testing ladder from computer testing to job-site deployment replaces one more piece of simulation with reality.
facts.quote: Each rung replaces one more piece of simulation with reality.

facts.text: Machines equipped with the existing warning system can record what their sensors saw.
facts.quote: Machines with the existing warning system can record what their sensors saw.

facts.text: Replay feeds recorded sensor data into new software to show whether the software would have detected a person; recorded data can test perception but not stopping.
facts.quote: Playing those recordings into the new software, called replay, shows whether it would have detected the person.

facts.text: Recorded-data replay is open loop because the recording does not change when the software decides to brake.
facts.quote: This is open loop: the recording does not change when the software decides to brake.

facts.text: Braking changes the future trajectory—the machine stops earlier and the person is somewhere else—and only closed-loop simulation can follow those changes.
facts.quote: Once the system brakes, the future changes (the machine stops earlier, the person is somewhere else), and only a closed-loop simulation can follow that.

facts.text: A model checked against measurements at 10 and 20 kilometers per hour on dry gravel is trusted between those speeds on dry gravel.
facts.quote: A model that has been checked against measurements at 10 and 20 kilometers per hour on dry gravel is trusted between those points, on that surface.

facts.text: For a model checked at 10 and 20 kilometers per hour on dry gravel, predictions on ice, at 30 kilometers per hour, or with a different sensor height are guesses outside the validity envelope.
facts.quote: Outside that envelope, on ice, at 30 kilometers per hour, with a different sensor height, its answers are guesses.

facts.text: Simulation-trust frameworks used in aerospace, medicine, nuclear power and car regulation all demand physical anchors, a stated validity envelope and honesty about uncertainty.
facts.quote: All of them demand physical anchors, a stated envelope, and honesty about uncertainty.

facts.text: The space shuttle Columbia was lost in 2003 partly because a model was used far outside its validity envelope.
facts.quote: The space shuttle Columbia was lost in 2003 partly because a model was used far outside its envelope.

facts.text: A loaded heavy machine on a downhill gravel road needs a long distance to stop.
facts.quote: A loaded machine on a downhill gravel road needs a long distance to stop

facts.text: Heavy-machine brakes take time to respond after a braking command.
facts.quote: the brakes take time to respond after the command.

facts.text: Required sensor detection range for a person is the stopping distance plus the distance traveled during delays, with reliable detection required in the worst conditions.
facts.quote: the distance needed to stop, plus the distance covered during the delays, is how far the sensor must see a person, reliably, in the worst conditions.

facts.text: If dust prevents the sensor from detecting a person at the required stopping range, the machine must drive slower or the system cannot promise to stop.
facts.quote: If the sensor cannot see that far in dust, the machine must drive slower or the system cannot promise to stop.
